title: Growing basil in containers
text:
Basil is a warm-season herb that grows well in containers on a sunny balcony or windowsill.
Light. Basil needs at least 6 hours of direct sunlight a day. With less light, the stems stretch and the leaves become small and pale.
Temperature. Basil is sensitive to cold. Growth slows when night temperatures drop below 10°C, and leaves can blacken below 5°C.
Watering. Water when the top 2 cm of soil feel dry to the touch. Pots in full sun may need water every day in summer.
Pinching. Pinch off the tip of each stem above a pair of leaves once the plant has 3 pairs of true leaves. This makes the plant branch and grow bushier.
Flowers. Remove flower buds as soon as they appear. Once basil flowers, the leaves become fewer and more bitter.
Containers. Use a pot at least 20 cm wide with drainage holes in the bottom.
